spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact scroll-axis-lock grammar with CSS.supports per value and reads the computed value back from a real element — not a broad CSS.supports existence check.

interactive.rationale: Element-type select re-runs the probe against different boxes; grammar table updates live.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Answers is-it-supported with the property itself, as the blurb frames it.

edge_cases.rationale: Invalid values probed alongside valid ones so the parser's acceptance set is visible.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite passes 6/6 on this build — the property is live here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Grammar probed correct on all cases (falsifiable assert grammar-probed passed); console clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: grammar-probed asserts correct === CASES.length — falsifiable and on-contract.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled select, aria-live output, visible focus 12/12.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 6px of horizontal overflow at 360px caused by the element-type select (right edge 366px) — small but measurable; everything else fits.

openQuestions.title: Clamp the element-type select at narrow widths
openQuestions.detail: At 360×740 DPR3 the select's intrinsic width (long option text: 'a scroll container (overflow: auto)…') pushes 6px past the viewport (measured right edge 366px). max-width:100% on the select (or width:100% within its label grid) removes the page's only overflow.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected. Property genuinely supported on this build and the probe is falsifiable; one 6px select overflow to clamp on mobile.
